functions.name: fast_float::from_chars
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename UC = char,
          typename = FASTFLOAT_ENABLE_IF(is_supported_float_type<T>::value)>
FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 from_chars_result_t<UC>
from_chars(UC const *first, UC const *last, T &value,
           chars_format fmt = chars_format::general) noexcept;
functions.description: Parses the character sequence [first,last) as a floating‑point number (locale‑independent, like C locale std::strtod) into value of type T (float/double etc.), returning the closest IEEE-754 value with round-to-even. On success, the returned ptr points just past the parsed number and ec is default-constructed; otherwise ec indicates the error. No exceptions or allocations. Formatting allowed is controlled by fmt (fixed/scientific/general).
requirements: T must satisfy is_supported_float_type<T>::value (e.g., float, double) at compile time.
first and last must delimit a valid accessible character range [first,last).
value must be a valid lvalue reference to T where the parsed result can be stored.
fmt controls which notations are accepted; by default chars_format::general allows both fixed and scientific.
The caller must check the returned from_chars_result_t<UC>::ec for errors before using value.
Parsing is locale-independent (expects C-locale formatting).
Function is noexcept; it will not throw. It does not allocate memory.

functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename UC = char>
FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 from_chars_result_t<UC>
from_chars_advanced(UC const *first, UC const *last, T &value,
                    parse_options_t<UC> options) noexcept;
functions.description: Parses the character sequence [first,last) into value using parsing behavior governed by options. Supports both floating‑point and integer types. Returns a from_chars_result with ptr at the first unparsed character and ec indicating success or error. No exceptions or allocations.
requirements: first and last must delimit a valid accessible character range [first,last).
value must be a valid lvalue reference to a type compatible with the provided options (exact constraints are not specified in this header).
options must be a valid parse_options_t<UC> instance; specific option semantics are not documented here.
The caller must check the returned from_chars_result_t<UC>::ec for errors before using value.
Function is noexcept; it will not throw. It does not allocate memory.

functions.name: fast_float::integer_times_pow10
functions.signature:
FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 inline double
integer_times_pow10(uint64_t mantissa, int decimal_exponent) noexcept;
functions.description: Computes mantissa * 10^decimal_exponent and returns the correctly rounded result as a double (round-to-nearest, ties-to-even), per IEEE-754. Returns +infinity on overflow and 0 on underflow. No exceptions or allocations.
requirements: mantissa is an unsigned 64-bit integer (non-negative).
decimal_exponent is a signed integer exponent for base-10 scaling (no specific bounds documented).
Caller should be prepared for infinity on overflow and 0 on underflow.
Function is noexcept; it will not throw. It does not allocate memory.

functions.name: fast_float::integer_times_pow10
functions.signature:
FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 inline double
integer_times_pow10(int64_t mantissa, int decimal_exponent) noexcept;
functions.description: Computes mantissa * 10^decimal_exponent and returns the correctly rounded result as a double (round-to-nearest, ties-to-even), per IEEE-754. Returns ±infinity on overflow (sign follows mantissa) and 0 on underflow. No exceptions or allocations.
requirements: mantissa is a signed 64-bit integer (may be negative).
decimal_exponent is a signed integer exponent for base-10 scaling (no specific bounds documented).
Caller should be prepared for infinity on overflow and 0 on underflow.
Function is noexcept; it will not throw. It does not allocate memory.

data_types.description: A character sequence representing a number in text form. May include optional leading sign (+/-), digits, optional decimal point and fractional part, optional exponent with 'e' or 'E' followed by an optional sign and digits (scientific notation). Whitespace or locale-specific formatting is not required/assumed; formatting is C-locale style. Examples: "0", "-123", "+4.56", "7.89e10", "-1e-3". For integer parsing, it may be just an optional sign and digits.
